title: Rigveda 7.78: To Usas
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.78: To Usas: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.78 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Usas. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 542r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.78.1-5 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 5, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 542r
translation.original_text:
1prati̍ ke̱tava̍ḥ pratha̱mā a̍dṛśrann ū̱rdhvā a̍syā a̱ñjayo̱ vi śra̍yante | uṣo̍ a̱rvācā̍ bṛha̱tā rathe̍na̱ jyoti̍ṣmatā vā̱mam a̱smabhya̍ṁ vakṣi ||
2prati̍ ṣīm a̱gnir ja̍rate̱ sami̍ddha̱ḥ prati̱ viprā̍so ma̱tibhi̍r gṛ̱ṇanta̍ḥ | u̱ṣā yā̍ti̱ jyoti̍ṣā̱ bādha̍mānā̱ viśvā̱ tamā̍ṁsi duri̱tāpa̍ de̱vī ||
3e̱tā u̱ tyāḥ praty a̍dṛśran pu̱rastā̱j jyoti̱r yaccha̍ntīr u̱ṣaso̍ vibhā̱tīḥ | ajī̍jana̱n sūrya̍ṁ ya̱jñam a̱gnim a̍pā̱cīna̱ṁ tamo̍ agā̱d aju̍ṣṭam ||
4ace̍ti di̱vo du̍hi̱tā ma̱ghonī̱ viśve̍ paśyanty u̱ṣasa̍ṁ vibhā̱tīm | āsthā̱d ratha̍ṁ sva̱dhayā̍ yu̱jyamā̍na̱m ā yam aśvā̍saḥ su̱yujo̱ vaha̍nti ||
5prati̍ tvā̱dya su̱mana̍so budhantā̱smākā̍so ma̱ghavā̍no va̱yaṁ ca̍ | ti̱lvi̱lā̱yadhva̍m uṣaso vibhā̱tīr yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
1WE have beheld her earliest lights approaching: her many glories part, on high, asunder. On car sublime, refulgent, wending hither, O Ushas, bring the Wealth that makes us happy.
2The fire well-kindIed sings aloud to greet her, and with their hymns the priests are chanting welcome. Ushas approaches in her splendour, driving all evil darkness far away, the Goddess.
3Apparent eastward are those lights of Morning, sending out lustre, as they rise, around them. She hath brought forth Sun, sacrifice, and Agni, and far away hath fled detested darkness.
4Rich Daughter of the Sky, we all behold her, yea, all men look on Dawn as she is breaking. fler car that moves self-harnessed hath she mounted, the car drawn onward by her well-yoked horses.
5Inspired with loving thoughts this day to greet thee, we and our wealthy nobles have awakened. Show yourselves fruitful, Dawns, as ye are rising. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 542r (numbered 63r by the scribe) (OPenn image 542, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.77.6 ‹divaḥ duhitaḥ vardhayanti uṣaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 542v (numbered 63v by the scribe), begins in RV 7.79.1 ‹-cakṣasā āvar ity āvaḥ›. Verses 7.78.1-5 end on this page.
